subject.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit

question: Should OpenClaw fix Groq's default TPM-limit failure with this exact Groq/model/error-scoped recovery, or establish a shared OpenAI-compatible transport policy that omits implicit output reservations?
rationale: Both paths can address the reported failure but encode different long-term compatibility contracts across providers, default requests, tool availability, and model capability metadata; source review cannot safely choose that product boundary alone.

options.title: Adopt the Groq-scoped recovery
options.body: Keep normal requests unchanged and retry only the exact Groq TPM 413 with a tool-free 1,024-token payload, preserving explicit user budgets.

options.title: Adopt a shared transport policy
options.body: Close or supersede this branch in favor of a separately reviewed transport-wide change that removes implicit output reservations across compatible providers.

options.title: Pause both approaches
options.body: Keep the issue and both PRs open until provider/runtime owners define the intended default output-budget contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt the Groq-scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Keep normal requests unchanged and retry only the exact Groq TPM 413 with a tool-free 1,024-token payload, preserving explicit user budgets.
